explanation: The I84V mutation reduces the hydrophobic packing surface within the S1/S1' subpocket by removing approximately 27 Ų of van der Waals contact volume, creating a cavity between the smaller valine side chain and atazanavir's corresponding binding surface. This loss of favorable hydrophobic interactions and van der Waals contacts at the 3.3 Å minimum distance destabilizes the inhibitor binding geometry without introducing compensatory interactions, as the mutation involves no charge change and only marginal hydrophobicity loss. Consequently, the protease accommodates atazanavir less favorably in this critical substrate-binding pocket, reducing overall binding affinity and conferring resistance.
